column1: # Declared value corrections for the free-text and controlled-vocabulary columns (#637, #633).
# One row per rewrite. `species` scopes it: a value that is correct under one species' symbol
# convention and wrong under another must not be rewritten globally. Empty `species` means every row
# carrying `from` in that column.
# The instrument is `out/reports/lookalikes.tsv`, which reports values differing from another value
# only in case or in a `-`, `_`, `.` or space. This file is the fix list; the report is what finds the
# next one. Nothing here is a gate, and it must not become one: a look-alike pair can be two strains,
# two serotypes, or one gene under two species' conventions.
# NOT corrected, deliberately, and each for a reason the report cannot know:
#   antigen.gene MBP (HomoSapiens) / Mbp (MusMusculus)     - HGNC capitalises, MGI title-cases. Both right.
#   antigen.gene G6PC2 (HomoSapiens) / G6pc2 (MusMusculus) - same convention, same reason.
#   antigen.gene NEF (InfluenzaA), 8 records                - influenza has no Nef; needs the paper, not a rule.
#   antigen.gene POL (HCV), 36 records                      - HCV's polyprotein is a separate question.
#   antigen.gene synthetic / Synthetic, 56 records          - not a gene at all (#633); a curation decision.
#   antigen.species AdV / HAdV5, 25 records                 - #633 proposes AdV -> HAdV5 and this file
#       does NOT do it, because the two spellings are not the same claim. Both carry `TDLGQNLLY`, the
#       conserved HLA-A*01 hexon epitope, which is used precisely because it is conserved across human
#       adenovirus species - so calling PMID:35401538's 12 records HAdV5 would assert a serotype its
#       source did not determine. And collapsing the other way would destroy a real one:
#       PMID:10671225's `SGPSNTPPEI` is E1A, which is Ad5-specific. One gene, two source labels; the
#       gene case is normalised below and the species split stays in `out/reports/epitope-sources.tsv`,
#       which is #633's own treatment for a conserved peptide.
# MOVED OUT of this file, to `proofreading/method_vocabulary.tsv`:
#   Every `method.identification` correction. That column is a comma-separated **set of tokens**, so
#   the unit of correction is the token and a whole-cell rewrite can only ever reach a variant that
#   happens to be a cell on its own. The four rows this file used to carry - `tetramer.sort`,
#   `Tetramer-sort`, `tetramer sort` and `antigen loaded targets, IFNg capture assay` - are all
#   declared there now, as token aliases, and produce the same cells. Two tables answering for one
#   column is the drift this file exists to prevent.
